subject: Private VPC pricing - licensing, support tiers, and environment count
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T14:10:00-08:00
Subject: Private VPC pricing - licensing, support tiers, and environment count

Hi Alice / Tom,

Great to meet earlier today - thanks for the time and for walking us through FinTechCo's use case for transaction enrichment and risk scoring. Quick recap and a few follow-ups we promised on the call: 

- Primary ask: Private/VPC deployment to satisfy data residency and isolation.
- Expected workload: batch enrichment + real-time scoring via API, a mix of generation and embeddings.
- Security: KMS for keys, SOC2 + additional audit evidence requested.

Follow-ups / asks for pricing: 
1) Can you confirm monthly token volumes (generation + embeddings) ranges you expect over the next 12 months? A baseline + burst peak is helpful.
2) Do you have a target unit economics (e.g., target $ / 1M tokens) or an annual budget range we should align to for license/support + per-token usage?
3) How many environments would you need initially (dev, staging, prod, DR), and do you require separate physical clusters for each?

I've attached a short "initial-pricing-options.pdf" with two licensing approaches (subscription + per-token and reserved capacity). Once we have the numbers above we'll surface a clear ballpark.

Propose a 30-minute follow-up once you confirm volumes - happy to bring Rishi (SE) for technical sizing.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachment: initial-pricing-options.pdf (pdf)
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@fintechco.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T09:34:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing - licensing, support tiers, and environment count

Ben - thanks for the note and for the clear recap. A few numbers from our side to help you model pricing: 

- Estimated monthly token volumes (current - 12 mo projection): 10M (low) - 30M (expected peak) tokens/month. This includes ~20% embeddings and 80% generation.
- Target unit economics: we'd like to model ~$2,500 / 1M tokens as a target for our CFO, but we understand private deployments can differ - please show sensitivity at $1,500 / 1M and $3,500 / 1M.
- Budget range: roughly $60k - $180k ARR for platform + support in Year 1 depending on terms.
- Environments: we need dev, staging, prod, and a DR environment. Prefer consolidated clusters if possible, but will need logical separation/namespaces.
- Support: Enterprise support (24x7 on-call escalation + quarterly business reviews).
- Compliance: we will need data residency in US-East and documentation for SOC2 + pen test evidence.

I'm attaching an internal requirements doc that might be useful.

If you can provide a simple pricing matrix (license + support tier + per-token scenarios at the three unit econ points) we'll review and iterate. Happy to do a 30-min call Friday afternoon - propose 2:00pm ET?

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Head of Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
alice.zhang@fintechco.com

Attachment: fintechco-internal-requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T11:10:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing - licensing, support tiers, and environment count

Alice - perfect, this is exactly what we need, thanks. 

I'll surface two clean options for you to review (ballparks below), and Rishi can confirm technical sizing assumptions: 

Option A - Annual license + per-token consumption
- Fixed annual platform license: $40k - $85k (covers runtime license + maintenance)
- Enterprise support add-on: $15k - $35k (24x7, SLA coverage, quarterly BRs)
- Per-token: modeled at $1,500 / 1M tokens (basic quantized models) up to $3,500 / 1M (higher-cost model / less quantization).

Option B - Reserved capacity (dedicated node pools)
- Annual reserved capacity: $65k - $140k depending on core GPU sizing and instance count. Includes base support (Standard); Enterprise support as add-on.
- Effective $ / 1M tokens depends heavily on batching and KV caching - ballpark $1,200 - $2,800 / 1M for typical retrieval/generation mixes.

Notes / assumptions:
- Numbers above assume 3 primary environments (dev/staging/prod) consolidated across namespaces with a single control plane to reduce overhead - adding dedicated physical clusters per env would add ~25-40% to license/reserved-cost.
- KMS + SOC2 evidence support included; pen test evidence requires legal / security LOE that we can scope.

I've attached a short "redwood-private-pricing-options.pdf" with a matrix.

Next step: Rishi - can you confirm the environment impact on licensing/reserved capacity and a rough CPU/GPU profile for 30M tokens/month with peak QPS of ~120 rps? Also Alice - is Friday 2:00pm ET still good for a quick review?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-pricing-options.pdf (pdf)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-15T12:02:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC pricing - licensing, support tiers, and environment count

Hi all - quick technical note on environment and cost sensitivity: 

- Environment count: Logical separation (namespaces) with a shared cluster is our recommended approach for cost efficiency. Physical separation (one cluster per env) typically increases base license/reserved capacity costs by ~25-40% because of minimum node footprints and redundancy requirements.
- Worker pools: For a 30M token/month profile with 120 peak QPS, plan for a modest reserved pool (2-4 A100-equivalent GPUs) for prod with autoscale for bursts; dev/staging can share smaller lower-cost nodes.
- Unit economics: With model quantization (int8) and prefix/KV caching enabled, expect effective unit costs closer to $1,200 - $1,800 / 1M tokens. If you need unquantized higher-accuracy models across the board, $2,800 - $3,500 / 1M is plausible.
- Support tiers: Standard = business hours + 24-hour response; Enterprise = 24x7 on-call, dedicated TAM, included runbooks and quarterly optimizations. Enterprise support also includes a higher RTO/RPO in the SLA.

Happy to run a quick sizing exercise on Friday - I can bring a short cluster/instance sketch to show the delta.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks Ben/Rishi - this is very helpful. Friday 2:00pm ET works for us. Confirming:
- Environments: dev, staging, prod, DR (prefer logical separation, single cluster).
- Support: Enterprise tier.
- Target: please include pricing rows for $1,500 / $2,500 / $3,500 per 1M token.
- Additional ask: include a short SOW template clause for data residency and KMS handling.

Looking forward to the call - please send calendar invite.

Best,
Alice
